questions.stem_md:
The side $AB$ of a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ is produced to $E$. The exterior angle $\angle CBE = (2x + 15)^\circ$ and the interior angle $\angle ADC = (4x - 35)^\circ$.

(i) Write an equation in $x$ and state the property used.

(ii) Find $x$.

(iii) Find $\angle ABC$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle, so $\angle CBE = \angle ADC$: $2x + 15 = 4x - 35$.

(ii) $2x + 15 = 4x - 35 \Rightarrow 50 = 2x \Rightarrow x = 25$.

(iii) $\angle CBE = 2 \times 25 + 15 = 65$, and $\angle ABC = 180 - 65 = 115$ (angles on the straight line $ABE$).

questions.stem_md:
$ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral with both diagonals drawn, $\angle ACB = 52^\circ$ and $\angle BAC = 40^\circ$.

(i) Find $\angle ADB$.

(ii) Find $\angle BDC$.

(iii) Hence find $\angle ADC$, and check it against $\angle ABC$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) $\angle ADB = \angle ACB = 52^\circ$, angles in the same segment of the chord $AB$.

(ii) $\angle BDC = \angle BAC = 40^\circ$, angles in the same segment of the chord $BC$.

(iii) $\angle ADC = \angle ADB + \angle BDC$: $52^\circ + 40^\circ = 92^\circ$. In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 52^\circ - 40^\circ = 88^\circ$, and $88^\circ + 92^\circ = 180^\circ$, as the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral should.

questions.stem_md: Prove that a parallelogram whose four vertices lie on a circle is a rectangle.

answer.model_answer_md:
Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram inscribed in a circle. In a parallelogram the opposite angles are equal: $\angle A = \angle C$.

$ABCD$ is also a cyclic quadrilateral, so its opposite angles are supplementary: $\angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ$.

Substituting $\angle C = \angle A$: $2\angle A = 180^\circ$, so $\angle A = 90^\circ$ and $\angle C = 90^\circ$.

Co-interior angles between the parallel sides add to $180^\circ$, so $\angle B = 180^\circ - \angle A = 90^\circ$ and $\angle D = 90^\circ$. All four angles are right angles, so $ABCD$ is a rectangle.

questions.solution_md: Equal opposite angles that are also supplementary must each be a right angle.

questions.stem_md: $A$ and $B$ are points of a circle with centre $O$, and $P$ is a point on the major arc $AB$ such that $O$ lies inside the angle $APB$. Prove that $\angle AOB = 2\angle APB$.

answer.model_answer_md:
Join $PO$ and produce it to meet the circle at $Q$. Put $\angle OPA = x$ and $\angle OPB = y$.

$OP = OA$ (radii), so $\angle OAP = \angle OPA = x$. $\angle AOQ$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle OAP$, so $\angle AOQ = x + x = 2x$.

In the same way, $OP = OB$ gives $\angle BOQ = 2y$.

Adding: $\angle AOB = \angle AOQ + \angle BOQ = 2x + 2y = 2(x + y) = 2\angle APB$.

questions.stem_md:
$A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are points of a circle with centre $O$. $C$ lies on the major arc $AB$, $D$ lies on the minor arc $AB$ and $\angle ACB = 41^\circ$. Show all working.

(a) Find $\angle AOB$ and state the property used.

(b) Find $\angle OAB$ and $\angle OBA$.

(c) Find $\angle ADB$ and show that $\angle ACB + \angle ADB = 180^\circ$. Which property of the quadrilateral $ACBD$ does this show?

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended at any point on the remaining part of the circle. So $\angle AOB = 2 \times 41^\circ = 82^\circ$.

**(b)** $OA = OB$ (radii), so $\triangle OAB$ is isosceles with $\angle OAB = \angle OBA$. Then $\angle OAB = \angle OBA = \dfrac{180^\circ - 82^\circ}{2} = 49^\circ$.

**(c)** $D$ is on the minor arc, so $ACBD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral with $C$ and $D$ opposite corners, and $\angle ADB = 180^\circ - 41^\circ = 139^\circ$. Check: $41^\circ + 139^\circ = 180^\circ$. The opposite angles of the cyclic quadrilateral $ACBD$ are supplementary.

questions.stem_md:
$ABCD$ is a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle, and $AB$ is a diameter. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ are drawn, $\angle CAB = 30^\circ$ and $\angle ABD = 36^\circ$. Show all working.

(a) Find $\angle ACB$, $\angle ADB$ and $\angle ABC$, giving a reason for each.

(b) Find $\angle BAD$ and $\angle BCD$.

(c) Find $\angle CAD$ and $\angle CBD$, and name the property that makes them equal.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** $AB$ is a diameter, so $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$ and $\angle ADB = 90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle). In $\triangle ABC$: $\angle ABC = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$.

**(b)** In $\triangle ABD$: $\angle BAD = 90^\circ - 36^\circ = 54^\circ$. $ABCD$ is cyclic, so $\angle BCD = 180^\circ - 54^\circ = 126^\circ$.

**(c)** $\angle CAD = \angle BAD - \angle BAC$: $54^\circ - 30^\circ = 24^\circ$. $\angle CBD = \angle CAD = 24^\circ$, because angles in the same segment of the chord $CD$ are equal. Check: $\angle ABC = \angle ABD + \angle DBC = 36^\circ + 24^\circ = 60^\circ$.

questions.stem_md:
$ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral with $\angle ABC = (4y + 6)^\circ$, $\angle ADC = (2y + 24)^\circ$ and $\angle DAB = 60^\circ$. The side $AB$ is produced to $P$ and the diagonal $AC$ is drawn. Show all working.

(a) Form an equation and find $y$. Hence write down $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ADC$.

(b) Find $\angle CBP$ and give the property used.

(c) If $\angle BAC = 24^\circ$, find $\angle ACB$, $\angle CAD$ and $\angle CBD$.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ADC$ are opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral, so they add up to $180^\circ$: $(4y + 6) + (2y + 24) = 180 \Rightarrow 6y + 30 = 180 \Rightarrow y = 25$. Then $\angle ABC = 4 \times 25 + 6 = 106$ and $\angle ADC = 2 \times 25 + 24 = 74$.

**(b)** The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle, so $\angle CBP = \angle ADC = 74^\circ$. (Also $\angle CBP = 180^\circ - 106^\circ = 74^\circ$.)

**(c)** In $\triangle ABC$: $\angle ACB = 180 - 106 - 24 = 50$. $\angle CAD = \angle DAB - \angle BAC = 60 - 24 = 36$. $\angle CBD = \angle CAD = 36^\circ$, angles in the same segment of the chord $CD$.

questions.solution_md: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180; the exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle; the angle sum of triangle ABC; angles in the same segment of CD.

questions.stem_md:
$ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral with $\angle DAB = 70^\circ$ and $\angle ABC = 95^\circ$. The sides $AB$ and $DC$ are produced beyond $B$ and $C$ to meet at $P$, and the sides $AD$ and $BC$ are produced beyond $D$ and $C$ to meet at $Q$. Show all working.

(a) Find $\angle BCD$ and $\angle ADC$.

(b) Find $\angle PCB$, $\angle PBC$ and $\angle BPC$.

(c) Find $\angle QDC$, $\angle DCQ$ and $\angle DQC$.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** $ABCD$ is cyclic, so opposite angles are supplementary: $\angle BCD = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$ and $\angle ADC = 180^\circ - 95^\circ = 85^\circ$.

**(b)** The exterior angle at $C$ (side $DC$ produced) equals the interior opposite angle: $\angle PCB = \angle DAB = 70^\circ$. The exterior angle at $B$ equals $\angle ADC$, so $\angle PBC = 85^\circ$. In $\triangle PBC$: $\angle BPC = 180^\circ - 70^\circ - 85^\circ = 25^\circ$.

**(c)** The exterior angle at $D$ (side $AD$ produced) equals the interior opposite angle $\angle ABC$, so $\angle QDC = 95^\circ$. The exterior angle at $C$ (side $BC$ produced) equals $\angle DAB$, so $\angle DCQ = 70^\circ$. In $\triangle QDC$: $\angle DQC = 180^\circ - 95^\circ - 70^\circ = 15^\circ$.

questions.stem_md:
The triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle with centre $O$ inside the triangle, with $\angle OAB = 28^\circ$ and $\angle OCB = 32^\circ$. $D$ is the mid-point of the minor arc $AC$ (the arc not containing $B$). Show all working.

(a) Find $\angle AOB$ and $\angle BOC$.

(b) Find $\angle ACB$, $\angle BAC$ and $\angle ABC$, and check that they add up to $180^\circ$.

(c) Find $\angle ADC$ and $\angle DAC$.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** $OA = OB$, so $\angle OBA = 28^\circ$ and $\angle AOB = 180^\circ - 2 \times 28^\circ = 124^\circ$. $OB = OC$, so $\angle OBC = 32^\circ$ and $\angle BOC = 180^\circ - 2 \times 32^\circ = 116^\circ$.

**(b)** The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre on the same arc: $\angle ACB = \dfrac{124^\circ}{2} = 62^\circ$ and $\angle BAC = \dfrac{116^\circ}{2} = 58^\circ$. Then $\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 62^\circ - 58^\circ = 60^\circ$, and $62^\circ + 58^\circ + 60^\circ = 180^\circ$.

**(c)** $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral, so $\angle ADC = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$. $D$ is the mid-point of the arc $AC$, so $DA = DC$ and $\angle DAC = \angle DCA = \dfrac{180^\circ - 120^\circ}{2} = 30^\circ$.

questions.stem_md:
In a quadrilateral $PQRS$ the diagonals $PR$ and $QS$ are drawn. $Q$ and $R$ lie on the same side of $PS$, and $\angle PQS = \angle PRS = 37^\circ$. Show all working.

(a) Show that $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ lie on one circle, giving the property used.

(b) Given that $\angle QPS = 98^\circ$, find $\angle QRS$.

(c) Given that $\angle PSR = 95^\circ$, find $\angle PQR$. The side $SR$ is produced to $X$; find $\angle QRX$ and name the property used.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** $Q$ and $R$ are on the same side of $PS$ and the chord $PS$ subtends equal angles $37^\circ$ at them. By the converse of the same-segment property, $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ lie on a circle.

**(b)** $PQRS$ is therefore cyclic, and $\angle QPS$ and $\angle QRS$ are opposite angles: $\angle QRS = 180^\circ - 98^\circ = 82^\circ$.

**(c)** $\angle PSR$ and $\angle PQR$ are opposite angles: $\angle PQR = 180^\circ - 95^\circ = 85^\circ$. The exterior angle at $R$ equals the interior opposite angle $\angle QPS$, so $\angle QRX = 98^\circ$. Check: $82^\circ + 98^\circ = 180^\circ$, so the angles at $R$ on the straight line $SRX$ are $82^\circ + 98^\circ = 180^\circ$.

questions.solution_md: Converse of angles in the same segment for concyclic points; opposite angles of the cyclic quadrilateral for QRS and PQR; the exterior angle at R equals the interior opposite angle QPS.

questions.stem_md:
In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ the diagonal $AC$ bisects the angle $\angle BAD$, and $\angle BAD = 84^\circ$. Show all working.

(a) Explain why $BC = CD$. Which property of a circle do you use?

(b) Find $\angle BCD$ and $\angle CBD$.

(c) Given that $\angle ABD = 46^\circ$, find $\angle ADB$, $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ADC$, and verify that $\angle ABC + \angle ADC = 180^\circ$.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** $\angle BAC = \angle CAD = \dfrac{84^\circ}{2} = 42^\circ$. These are angles at the circumference standing on the chords $BC$ and $CD$. Equal angles at the circumference stand on equal arcs, and equal arcs have equal chords, so $BC = CD$.

**(b)** $\angle BCD = 180^\circ - 84^\circ = 96^\circ$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral). $BC = CD$, so $\angle CBD = \angle CDB$ and $\angle CBD = \dfrac{180^\circ - 96^\circ}{2} = 42^\circ$. This agrees with $\angle CBD = \angle CAD = 42^\circ$, angles in the same segment of the chord $CD$.

**(c)** In $\triangle ABD$: $\angle ADB = 180^\circ - 84^\circ - 46^\circ = 50^\circ$. $\angle ABC = \angle ABD + \angle DBC = 46^\circ + 42^\circ = 88^\circ$ and $\angle ADC = \angle ADB + \angle BDC = 50^\circ + 42^\circ = 92^\circ$. Then $88^\circ + 92^\circ = 180^\circ$, as the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral must.
